attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post, not part of the embedded tweets.

semantics.note: 'Will take more than a decade' and 'absolute fantasy' are firm, unhedged language. The decade window ties to Amodei's under-10-year claim. 'Some other things' is rightly left unscored.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary. It treats eradication as ending cancer as a disease burden and cure as broad cures across mental illness, with a 2036-11-12 deadline. The contradiction wording for a mixed outcome is clumsy, but it is not unfair.

evidence.note: The NCI page says there are over 100 cancer types. That bears only on the factual premise, not on either forecast outcome.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast with a deadline about ten years after publication. The evaluation date is well before 2036-11-12, and the evidence shows no conclusive early event (cancer eradicated or mental illness broadly cured). The forecast cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Marcus says 'we don't have the data' in his own voice, introducing Rich Law's tweet. The tweet's '<1%' figure is not his claim and is correctly excluded.

semantics.note: This is a present-state claim, tied to his preceding sentence about the field being in no position to meet Amodei's timeline. The required data are unspecified, which makes the claim vague but still a firm assertion.

contract.note: The plain reading (data insufficient now for the stated cure goal) is ordinary. Requiring the evidence to account for feasible new data generation slightly raises the bar, but it does not change the result here.

evidence.note: A March 2025 editorial notes data gaps for virtual-cell models alongside extensive existing data. It predates the snapshot and does not link the gaps to the four-disease cure timeline.

reviews.rationale: The only evidence item shows that some biological data gaps exist. It does not establish whether available data are sufficient or insufficient for the stated cure goal at the publication-date snapshot, and no item contradicts the claim. The packet does not settle it.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence rejecting Amodei's prediction as reported in the embedded tweet.

semantics.note: 'Is not going to happen' is a firm forecast. The four diseases and the under-10-year timeline come from context, and the 'anything remotely like' qualifier is preserved.

contract.note: Negating the combined promise (support if any one category still lacks broad cures) is a fair logical reading. The 2036-11-12 deadline leaves the 'remotely like' extension unscored, as the contract admits. The contract is labelled 'retrospective' even though this is a forecast, which is an inconsistency.

evidence.note: FDA's 2024 approval of Kisunla as an Alzheimer's treatment. It is a regulator record mislabelled as a company disclosure, and it shows a treatment, not a cure. It does not settle the forecast.

reviews.rationale: This is a firm forecast whose decade window ends around 2036. The evidence shows no conclusive early event (validated broad cures across all four disease categories). The deadline has not passed, so the forecast cannot be scored.

attribution.note: He credits researchers ('as several researchers noted') but states the claim in his own voice ('we simply can't'), so he endorses it.

semantics.note: A firm present-tense claim about a feasibility constraint. It borders on a forecast, but treating it as an observation of the state at publication is defensible. Intensifiers and the qualifier are kept.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair. However, 'the degree that would be required' is unquantified, and candidate drugs and cure endpoints are unspecified, so the result depends on how those gaps are filled.

evidence.note: A 2018 FDA page giving typical trial phase lengths. It does not establish an unavoidable minimum duration.
FDA's accelerated approval page: surrogate endpoints shorten approval, but confirmatory trials are still required. It neither proves nor disproves the claim.
April 2026 FDA real-time trials initiative that may reduce gaps between phases. These are proofs of concept with no measured end-to-end timelines.
September 2026 FDA draft guidance on single pivotal trials and master protocols. These are acceleration mechanisms, not proof that cures can fit the window.

reviews.rationale: The FDA materials describe both standard trial durations and active acceleration efforts. None of them establishes either that the needed testing cannot be compressed into the under-decade window or that it can. The packet's listed counterevidence is only context, so the claim stays unresolved.
